AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Post-operative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia occurring after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Arrhythmia leads to prolonged hospitalization and may have impact on both short-term and long-term prognoses.

AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: The aim of this paper was the evaluation of the incidence of POAF in patients after CABG as well as the identification of its predictors.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The study was performed on 791 patients (selected from a group of 1031 patients who underwent CABG in the Clinical Department of Cardiology in years 2009-2011) who did not suffer from atrial fibrillation (AF) prior to isolated CABG. Data on co-existing diseases, as well as data collected at the time of surgery and in the post-operative period, were evaluated.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The average age of patients in the examined group was 64.6 (±9.1) years. Emergency CABG was performed on 38% of patients, whereas 75.1% of patients underwent CABG with theuse of extracorporealcirculation (ECC). Based on the incidence of POAF, the post-CABG patients were classified into POAF(+) group consisting of 166 (21%) patients, and POAF(-) group consisting of 625 (79%) patients. The first occurrence of arrhythmia during the first three days after surgery was observed in 76.5% of patients. The average age of POAF(+) and POAF(-) patients was 68.7 (±8.8) and 63.5 (±8.9) years, respectively; p<0.0001. Therespective incidence rates of co-existing diseases in patients with POAF and those without POAF were asfollows: arterial hypertension, 80.1% vs. 75.8%, p=0.2905; heart failure, 18.7% vs. 21.1%, p=0.5589; type 2 diabetes, 24.1% vs. 26.2%, p=0.6445. Stable angina pectoris was diagnosed in 22.3% of patients with POAF and 15% of patients without POAF, p=0.0344. Thefollowing conditions were more frequently indicated in patients with POAF than in those without POAF: low cardiac outputsyndrome, 28.9% vs. 14.2%, p<0.0001; cardiac tamponade, 9% vs. 4.6%, p=0.0439. Redbloodcell transfusions were performed more often in patients with POAF compared to those without POAF, the respective values being 70.5% vs. 55.7%, p=0.0008. Multivariate analysis revealed the following potential predictors of POAF: age≥70years (HR2.3), preoperativestableanginapectoris (HR 1.7), and post-CABG low cardiac output syndrome (HR 1.8).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: POAF was diagnosed in 21% of post-CABG patients, the major predictors were: age ≥70 years, preoperative stable angina as well as low cardiac output syndrome following CABG.
